newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks end down as investors await interims.
newsitem.headline: China stocks end down as investors await interims.

text.p: China's stock markets slipped lower on Wednesday as investors headed for the sidelines to await further announcements of 1997 interim results.
Only a few hard currency B share companies and domestic currency A share firms have announced their interim results so far with the remainder required to report by the end of August.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index closed lower in lacklustre trading as investors turned away from the market to await fresh incentives, brokers said.
With the reporting season for 1997 interim results just under way, investors were waiting to see how individual companies fared before trading actively, they said.
The B index fell 0.366 points or 0.47 percent to 76.966 points on volume of 8.780 million shares worth $4.353 million.
The recent strength of China plays listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange had also caused foreign investors to shift their attention away from Shanghai B shares, they said.
Foreign investors had pulled their money out of Southeast Asian stock markets due to worries over local currencies, brokers said.
That money had gone into Hong Kong, pushing up share prices there and making that market look attractive, they said.
Of Shanghai's 45 B shares, 43 traded with 20 down, 15 unchanged and eight up.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles Co Ltd was the biggest B share loser due to speculative selling. It fell $0.010 or 6.76 percent to $0.138.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares fell as investors took profits and settled down to wait for fresh news, brokers said.
The A index closed down 9.809 points or 0.78 percent at 1,244.911 points on volume of 503.530 million shares worth 6.211 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 26.276 points or 0.68 percent to 3,844.676 points.
Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed Wednesday slightly down in thin trade, with investors waiting for interim reports, brokers said.
The B index inched down 0.09 points or 0.06 percent to 132.73 points as turnover shrank to HK$39 million from Tuesday's HK$56 million.
The Chinese yuan-based A share index slipped 3.64 points or 0.88 percent to 409.59 on turnover of 7.1 billion yuan against Tuesday's 7.0 billion.
"The B index fell in narrow-band fluctuation while investors poked around for fresh talk about the company reports," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Buyers were concentrating on companies expected to post strong profits in their first-half 1997 reports as the August 30 deadline for listed firms to publish interim results drew near, analysts said.
Colour television maker Shenzhen Huafa Electronics Co Ltd was the biggest B share loser and slumped HK$0.28 or 8.54 percent to HK$3.00.
